2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 11-02-2020 at about 9.15 a.m., when the petitioner was riding his motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.TN-70-V-7778 on Hosuru-Bengaluru, NH-07 Road from Hosur towards Bengaluru and when reached near Bommasandra Fly over, on the left side of the road in a slow and cautiously, at that time a Lorry, bearing Reg.No.KA-44-0165 was moving in front of motor cycle, at that time suddenly took the Lorry to the right side of the road without giving any signal or indication.

Due to terrible impact, the motor cycle which was coming in the same direction came in contact with the backside hind portion of the said lorry and the rider fell down along with motor cycle and petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately, after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital for treatment, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 11.02.2020 to 02.03.2020, it was diagnosed that petitioner sustained grievous injuries i.e. 1) Head Injury with left fronto temporal contusion involving left internal capsular region

2)
Comminuted fracture of right maxilla involving the right orbit and other injuries all over the body.

He underwent operation i.e., Electrive tracheostomy under G.A on 13.02.2020 and OMFS procedure - ORIF right, maxilla and soft tissue injury repair was done under GA on 14.02.2020 and discharged on 02.03.2020 with an advice to come for followup treatment.

3. It is further submitted that Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
working as Accounts Executive at Maple tree Farms Pvt.Ltd., Devaganahappli and earning a sum of Rs.7,098/- per month.
He was an agriculturist, owning agricultural land out of that he was earning Rs.5,00,000/- p.a.

The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent manner of driving of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-44-0615 and in this connection the Hebbagodi police have registered a case in their crime No.54/2020, after investigation the said police have filed charge sheet against the said driver for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The second respondent being the R.C.Owner and the second respondent being the Insurer of the said Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-44-0615.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable for payment of compensation.
4. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court but only Respondent No.1 has filed the objections to main petition.
In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.2 had not appeared before the Tribunal and has been placed exparte.

sentences.text: It is held that - "Negligence - Truck suddenly took a right turn without giving any signal or indication, a car running behind on the adjacent lane hit against the truck and driver of car sustained fatal injuries - Defence that driver of truck took right turn slowly and carefully after giving indication and deceased negligently dashed her car against the truck and if not, accident occurred due to contributory negligence of both vehicles -

Eyewitness in his complaint to police stated that truck driver suddenly took right turn and car behind it hit right front portion of the truck- Insurance company failed to examine the truck driver or complainant or any eyewitness in support of its defence-Police laid charge-sheet against driver of truck -Tyre marks in the sketch and spot mahazar show that driver of truck took right turn from the left side of the car-Tribunal held that accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of truck."
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver or owner of the offending lorry.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited and above citations relied by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.
No.KA-44/0165 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the "Affirmative".

sentences.text: 32. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.81,294/- (27,098/- x 3) under this head.
33. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
As per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.5 for 21 days and as per Ex.P.6 for 1 days, in total he took treatment as an inpatient for 22 days.

Therefore, this tribunal inclines to award Rs. 33,000/- under this head.
34. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - bill receipt amounting to Rs.6,92,426/-.
Though Insurance Company disputed the medical expenses, nothing has been elicited during cross examination.

sentences.text: that Evidence - Appreciation of - Medical bills and vouchers - Large number of medical bills and vouchers were produced by claimant who was injured in accident towards surgeries conducted upon her and payment made to various hospitals and nursing homes along with purchase of medicines-Some of the documents were marked in evidence and some other documents were subjected to by counsel for insurance company for making them exhibits without raising tenable objections

- Tribunal neither upheld nor rejected the objection raised but has taken those documents into consideration while awarding pecuniary damages - Whether Tribunal was justified in accepting those vouchers in the absence of rebuttal evidMotor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149 (2) (a) (ii) -
Motor insurance - Driving licence - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - Minibus turned turtle and a passenger sustained injuries - driver of offending minibus had no valid licence at the time of accident - Whether insurance company is liable - Held ; no., insurance company directed to pay the compensation to claimant and recover the amount from owner and driver of the minibus.ence."
